votes.title: Resolution urging support for rent stabilization to protect tenants and preserve community stability
votes.summary: Resolution sponsored by Councilor McClain expressing City Council support for a proposed statewide initiative petition and legislation that would enable cities and towns to adopt rent stabilization (limiting annual rent increases to CPI or 5 percent, whichever is lower, with exemptions including owner-occupied buildings of four or fewer units and newly constructed housing), and requesting the City Clerk transmit copies to state officials. Motion made by Councilor McClain and seconded by Councilor Hogan to grant.
votes.result: Passed 10-0 (Councilor Dr. Meaney absent at vote)

transparency_notes: Attendance is recorded as "11 Councilors Present" at the start of the meeting (full 11-member council), so no one is listed absent for the meeting as a whole. However, Councilor Dr. Meaney is recorded as "ABSENT AT VOTE" on every Ways and Means transfer vote and on the rent stabilization resolution; the minutes do not state when he left. On the $390,000 Cannabis Fund transfer, the parenthetical reads "(Councilor Meaney absent, Avery ABSTAINED" with no closing parenthesis; Councilor Avery's abstention is recorded only on that item. Many transfer items print the line "Emergency Preamble was adopted by the following yea and nay vote:" twice in a row — an apparent duplication in the document. Several motions were recorded with no tally: acceptance of the May 12, 2026 minutes, setting down the National Grid public hearings, and all committee report acceptances ("REPORT ACCEPTED"). The adjournment motion (made by Councilor Net, seconded by Councilor Megie-Maddrey) has no recorded outcome. A citation for Pedro Diaz (Councilor McClain) is listed under New Business with no recorded vote, so it is not included in the votes list. In the Licensing committee section, one heading reads "UTO REPAIR/AUTO BODY/FLAMMABLE LICENSE RENEWAL," an apparent typo for "AUTO REPAIR." The three items paying money "to" departments ($300,693 Summer Youth Works Jobs; $599,500 FY26 Mass CEC Youth Equity Workforce Program; $19,400 FY26 Building EC Partnership FC612 Program) do not state a funding source in the minutes.
